definitions.explanation: Describes a situation where the timing is bad or one encounters an inconvenient coincidence.
Feeling uncomfortable or embarrassed because of an unfortunate encounter or situation.

examples.japanese: {間|ま}が{悪|わる}いことに{雨|あめ}が{降|ふ}ってきた。
examples.english: Unfortunately, it started to rain at the worst time.

examples.japanese: {間|ま}が{悪|わる}く、{店|みせ}はもう{閉|し}まっていた。
examples.english: As bad luck would have it, the store had already closed.

examples.japanese: {間|ま}が{悪|わる}いときに{電話|でんわ}が{鳴|な}って、{会議|かいぎ}が{中断|ちゅうだん}された。
examples.english: The phone rang at the worst possible moment and the meeting was interrupted.

examples.japanese: {悪口|わるぐち}を{言|い}っているところを{本人|ほんにん}に{聞|き}かれて{間|ま}が{悪|わる}かった。
examples.english: I felt awkward because the person overheard me talking badly about them.

examples.japanese: {元|もと}カノに{偶然|ぐうぜん}{会|あ}って{間|ま}が{悪|わる}かった。
examples.english: I ran into my ex-girlfriend by chance and it was awkward.

examples.japanese: {嘘|うそ}をついたのがばれて、{非常|ひじょう}に{間|ま}が{悪|わる}い{思|おも}いをした。
examples.english: My lie was found out and I felt terribly embarrassed.

notes:
USAGE:
Sense 1 describes bad timing or unfortunate coincidences, often used with ことに as {間|ま}が{悪|わる}いことに (as bad luck would have it). Sense 2 describes the feeling of embarrassment when caught in an uncomfortable situation.

CONTRAST:
- {間|ま}がいい (good timing; lucky) is the positive counterpart
- {気|き}まずい focuses more on interpersonal awkwardness, while {間|ま}が{悪|わる}い emphasizes the element of bad timing
